source.text: ወእምህየ፡ ሖርኩ፡ ማእከለ፡ ምድር፡ ወርኢኩ፡ *መካነ፡ ቡሩከ፡ [ጥሉለ፡] (ዘቦቱ፡ ዕፀወ፡) ዘቦቱ፡ አዕፁቀ፡ ዘይነብር፡ ወይሠርፅ፡ [እምዕፅ፡ ዘ*ተመተረ።]
source.note: Selected botanical wording and bracket/parenthesis boundaries retained. Moist is not shaded; branch-family spelling is not silently normalized. No named geographic or theological identification supplied.

transcription_uncertainties.detail: English preserves bracket/parenthesis boundaries and explicit moist/branch/cut-tree meanings; not a fresh manuscript or modern geography claim.

translation.text: From there I went to the middle of the earth and saw a blessed place, [moist], (where there were trees), with branches that remain and sprout [from a tree that has been cut].[a]

footnotes.text: The selected edition brackets the moist/dew-covered word and the final from-a-cut-tree phrase, and puts the trees clause in parentheses; those editorial boundaries remain visible in English. Moist follows the actual primary Dillmann1865 column1214 range, not the different shade-word family. The branch/twig family is supported by the actual column1019 entry ዐጽቅ and its plural forms; the selected inflected source spelling is retained, not normalized to the headword. Remain, sprout and cut follow actual primary columns651,246 and184–185. Charles printed64 notes21–22 describe editorial/gloss dependencies; this is selected edited wording, not a fresh manuscript collation. No named city, sanctuary, fig tree or tree-of-life identification is added.

source.text: ወበህየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ ደብረ፡ ቅዱሰ፡ ወመትሕተ፡ ደብር፡ ማይ፡ እመንገለ፡ ጽባሕ፡ ወ*ውሕዘቱ፡ መንገለ፡ ሰሜን።
source.note: Selected holy mountain, under-mountain water and east/north flow relations retained without identifying a modern site.

translation.text: There I saw a holy mountain, and beneath the mountain water from the east, and its flow toward the north.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected water phrase is from the east, using the morning/east direction family, followed by its northward flow. Actual primary columns1277–1278 and334–335 control the direction words, and columns892–893 control the flow word. North is the chosen directional rendering, not a validation of a modern map or a named mountain, city, spring or temple.

source.text: ወርኢኩ፡ መንገለ፡ ጽባሕ፡ *ካልአ፡ ደብረ፡ ዘይነውኅ፡ እምዝ፡ ወማእከሎሙ፡ ቈላ፡ ዕሙቀ፡ ወ*አልቦ፡ ርሐበ፡ ወ*ቦቱኒ፡ ማይ፡ የሐውር፡ መንገለ፡ ደብር።
source.note: Selected starred comparison and water-toward-mountain construction retained; exact landscape referents are not reconstructed.

transcription_uncertainties.detail: Height/extension comparison and flow toward a mountain retained; precise landscape referents not reconstructed.

translation.text: I saw another mountain toward the east, higher than this one. Between them [was] a deep ravine without breadth, and water in it flowed toward the mountain.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected comparison is higher/more extended than this one, not a silently substituted lower comparison. The ravine is literally without breadth. The last relation is water moving toward the mountain; no modern tributary route or exact mountain referent is reconstructed. The selected stars and the qualified wording remain essential. The bracketed English copula supplies grammar only, not an additional source verb.

source.text: ወመንገለ፡ ዐረቡ፡ ለዝ፡ ካልእ፡ ደብር፡ ወይትሕት፡ ሎቱ፡ ወአልቦ፡ ⟦?⟧፡ ወቈላ፡ ታሕት፡ ማእከሎሙ፡ ወአልእት፡ ቈላ፡ ዕሙቅ፡ ወይበስ፡ መንገለ፡ ጽንፈ፡ ሠለስቲሆሙ።

translation.text: To the west of this [was] another mountain, lower than it, and without ⟦unresolved word⟧; [there was] a valley below between them, and another deep, dry valley near the edge of the three of them.[a]

footnotes.text: This entire unit remains held. The actual selected sentence crosses PDF102 to104 and explicitly continues with mountain, lower-than-it, valley and deep/dry relations; the former clipped prefix is not a full source unit. The word after the negative has not passed my exact-fidel and lexical checks and is represented by a modern unresolved marker, not an ancient lacuna. The English displays the complete remaining clause order but is not publication-approved; no missing word is supplied from Greek or a familiar translation.

source.text: ወኵሉ፡ ቈላት፡ ዕሙቃት፡ ወ*አልቦን፡ ርኅበ፡ እምኵኵሕ፡ ጽኑዕ፡ ወዕፅ፡ ኢይትከል፡ ላዕሌሆን።
source.note: Selected narrow/deep/hard-rock wording and edition-added negative retained; no-tree-planted is not a claim that all vegetation or planting capability is absent.

transcription_uncertainties.detail: Actual printed66 note15 identifies negative addition with comparison dependency. English selected no-tree-planted is qualified, not broadened to all vegetation or physical impossibility.

translation.text: All the ravines were deep and narrow, of hard rock, and no tree was planted on them.[a]

footnotes.text: Narrow represents the selected without-breadth expression. Charles1906 printed66 note15 identifies the negative as an editorial addition in accordance with Greek and reports differing Ethiopic evidence; the actual selected negative is retained. No tree was planted does not mean that every kind of vegetation was absent or that planting was physically impossible. The hard-rock wording is not an independent geological or geographic certificate.

source.text: ወአንከርኩ፡ በእንተ፡ ኵኵሕ፡ ወ*አንከርኩ፡ በእንተ፡ ቈላ፡ ወጥቀ፡ አንከርኩ።
source.note: Selected threefold wonder, including starred repetition, retained. Valley/ravine remains a lexical range, not a named place.

translation.text: I marveled at the rocks, and I marveled at the valley, and I marveled greatly.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected term can be rendered valley or ravine. All three expressions of wonder are retained, including the starred repetition in the source; no named geological site or additional vision is supplied.
